entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper of C. G. Pop, G. C. Rad and G. C. Țurcaș on the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups of rank three. An incidence identity of degree t of a sequence is a family of coefficients indexed by its zero-sum subsequences whose sum is one and whose moments of degree 1 to t vanish. Theorem A (a transfer principle): if every sequence of L(t) terms over a finite abelian group Q has such an identity over F_p, or over the integers, then D(Q ⊕ H) ≤ L(D(H) − 1) for every finite abelian p-group H. Theorem B: for m = 2, 3, 4, every sequence of m(t + 3) − 2 terms over C_m^3 has an integral identity of degree t, and the invariant κ_t(C_m^3; K) equals m(t + 3) − 2 for every field K of characteristic zero or prime to m. Corollary C: D(C_{mp^a} ⊕ C_{mp^b} ⊕ C_{mp^c}) = m(p^a + p^b + p^c) − 2 for m = 2, 3, 4, every prime p not dividing m and 0 ≤ a ≤ b ≤ c; in particular D(C_15^3) = 43 and D(C_20^3) = 58. All lemmas, propositions, theorems and corollaries of the paper are formalized. The computer-assisted Lemmas 5.1(1) and 5.3 are checked by Lean's kernel, and every result depends only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three

entries.abstract: Formal statements and proofs, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of the results of F. Najman, "The Diophantine equation x⁴ ± y⁴ = iz² in Gaussian integers" (Amer. Math. Monthly 117 (2010)). In the Gaussian integers ℤ[i], the equation x⁴ − y⁴ = iz² has only trivial solutions (xyz = 0); the nontrivial solutions of x⁴ + y⁴ = iz² with gcd(x, y, z) = 1 are exactly those with x, y ∈ {±1, ±i} and z = ±i(1 + i), and all its nontrivial solutions are given by x ∈ {±y, ±iy}, z = ±i(1 + i)y²; and the equations x⁴ ± y⁴ = z² have only trivial solutions (a theorem of Hilbert, reproved in the paper). As the paper remarks, the same holds over ℚ(i). The proofs go through the elliptic curves y² = x³ + x and y² = x³ − x over ℚ(i), whose groups of ℚ(i)-points, the point at infinity included, are formalized as ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 and ℤ/2 × ℤ/4. Where the paper computes the ranks with a computer program, the formalization determines the ℚ(i)-points directly: the line through a point and its complex conjugate reduces them to rational points, which Fermat's descent determines. 9 theorems and 2 definitions, no sorry, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: The Diophantine equation x⁴ ± y⁴ = iz² in Gaussian integers

entries.abstract:
We realize Di Paola and Heller’s objective to give an algebraic account of generalized incompleteness theorems in recursion categories. From two disjoint domains of partial morphisms on the same object in a recursion category we construct a first-order theory internal to that category. Its nonlogical axioms assert the nullary predicates indexed by the first domain and the negations of those indexed by the second. If the generated theory is consistent, the two domains are inseparable if and only if every consistent closed internal extension of the theory in the same language is incomplete.
On pairs generating consistent theories, this construction is left adjoint to the functor that takes a consistent theory to its theorem and refutation subobjects. A second construction associates to a consistent theory the Turing category of partial maps in the slice over its theorem object. With deduction in parameter slices and a chosen global logical theorem, passage to the constant family in this category preserves and reflects essential incompleteness.
In the completed syntactic recursion category for Peano arithmetic (PA), one total morphism, interpreted on the natural numbers, takes an index for any computably enumerable axiomatization of a consistent extension of PA to the code of a sentence independent of that extension. For a Miller sequence, we expand the theory of real closed ordered fields by constants naming its terms and axioms giving their strict rational bounds. Every consistent extension is incomplete if one oracle program semidecides its axioms from every binary representation of the sequence. A cosheaf on a three-point space yields a propositional theory at each endpoint with no complete consistent extension in the same language having computably enumerable axioms.
The three statements selected for this entry are the inseparability criterion for the generated theory, the construction of a complete consistent extension from a Boolean assignment, and the existence of an inseparable pair whose generated theory is essentially incomplete.
entries.title: Logical consequence and essential incompleteness in recursion categories

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof about an algorithm (SPoIF, Secure Posts on Increasing Fence) that computes the relative neighborhood graph of N points of the unit cube in three dimensions. The points are binned into a grid of about N cells. For each point p, a cube of grid cells around p (the fence) grows until the points collected inside it cut every patch of its surface off from p: a patch is cut off by a collected point q when it lies beyond the plane through q with normal q - p, so that q lies in the lune of p and any point beyond the patch. The neighbours of p are then found among the collected points by the direct lune test. Two theorems are proved. Correctness: for any points of the cube, the neighbours reported at each point are exactly its neighbours in the relative neighborhood graph. Expected linear time: for N independent uniform points of the cube, the expected operation count of the whole algorithm is at most C N for a constant C.
entries.title: Expected linear time for the relative neighborhood graph of uniform points in the unit cube

entries.abstract: Complete Lean 4 formal proofs of two conjectures by Zhi-Wei Sun (2011) on OEIS A189286, defined by a(n) = (sum_{k=0}^n C(6k,3k) C(3k,k) C(6(n-k),3(n-k)) C(3(n-k),n-k)) / ((2n-1) C(3n,n)). This combined submission proves two distinct results: (1) an independent, self-contained elementary proof of the previously proved integrality conjecture (conjecture_1; earlier proved in T. Adamczewski, arXiv:2608.11941), via termwise p-adic divisibility using Legendre's formula and a 3-adic lifting argument; and (2) an original proof of Conjecture (ii) (conjecture_3: for every n >= 1, 8 divides a(n) and a(n)/8 is odd iff n is a power of two), via Kummer's theorem, binary submask counting, and a fixed-point-free involution mod 4. As of November 2026, conjecture_3 was listed without proof on OEIS A189286 and marked research open in FormalConjectures/OEIS/189286.lean, though no exhaustive literature search is claimed to rule out other proofs.
entries.title: Formal Proof of OEIS A189286 Integrality and 2-adic Divisibility Conjectures

entries.abstract: For all sufficiently large n there is an n-vertex split graph that stays connected after removing any set of fewer than ceiling(n/5) vertices. Its exact edge-clique partition number exceeds the fractional optimum by at least a positive constant times n^2 (log n)^(-5/2) times exp(-2 sqrt(log(24/7) log n)). The same lower bound holds with the fractional optimum restricted to cliques of order at most four. The construction combines a local triangle-packing obstruction, a signed weight estimate on affine blocks, and host assignments in a split graph.
entries.title: Nearly Quadratic Additive Gaps for Edge-Clique Partitions of Split Graphs

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof of the Nowakowski-Winkler theorem in the game of cops and robbers: a finite graph has cop number 1 if and only if it is dismantlable. A vertex u is a corner if some other vertex w has N[u] contained in N[w] (closed neighbourhoods), and a graph is dismantlable if corners can be deleted one at a time until one vertex is left. The proof defines a one-cop game played inside a vertex set, with a bridge lemma showing that on the whole vertex set it is exactly Formal Conjectures' game CopsCatchWithin with one cop. A general shadow-map lemma says that if f maps S into T, sends legal moves to legal moves, and a cop on f x can reach every vertex the robber can step to from x, then a cop that wins on T also wins on S, by chasing the robber's shadow f r. Folding a corner onto the vertex that covers it is such a map, so induction on dismantlability gives one direction. For the converse, following the robber's longest escape gives a corner just before capture: the robber's vertex, covered by the cop's. Folding that corner away is a retract, and a cop that wins on a set also wins on any retract of it by standing on the image of its position, so induction on the number of vertices shows every cop-win finite graph is dismantlable. As a corollary, every finite nonempty tree is dismantlable (each leaf is a corner covered by its neighbour) and so has cop number 1. This is the statement meyniel_conjecture.variants.tree of Formal Conjectures, which marks it research solved. The mathematics is classical and no mathematical priority is claimed; to our knowledge this is the first published Lean 4 formalisation.
entries.title: Cop-win graphs are exactly the dismantlable graphs (Nowakowski-Winkler), and trees have cop number 1

entries.abstract: The diagonal Ramsey number R(12,12) is at least 1661: there is a simple graph on 1660 vertices such that neither the graph nor its complement contains a clique on 12 vertices, that is, a red/blue colouring of the edges of K_1660 with no monochromatic K_12. The graph is built from the Mathon–Shearer (11,11)-colouring M(797) on 1596 vertices by deleting a set of 21 vertices, which contains two antipodal pairs of M(797), and adding 85 core vertices, each of which copies a deleted vertex or has a single colour towards the remaining 1575 vertices. The proof is a clone-projection argument with an antipodal rule. It uses that M(797) has no monochromatic K_11 (proved in Lean here, following r1212-1642), that antipodal vertices of M(797) have opposite colours towards every other vertex, and finite checks on the 85 core vertices that the Lean kernel evaluates with decide +kernel. The construction and the proof are described in the preprint hexagon:2611.00248. This repository is a port of the formalization in https://github.com/YueMa0/r1212-1661 (Lean 4.32.1) to Lean 4.35.0 and the module system.
entries.title: R(12,12) ≥ 1661: a red/blue colouring of the edges of K_1660 with no monochromatic K_12

entries.abstract: Conditional on the two interval verifications of Appendix A, this Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization proves Theorem 1.1 of the paper. For every offspring law with no mass at zero and mean 1 < m < ∞, the speed v of the λ-biased random walk on the Bienaymé tree, constructed as the almost-sure limit of |X_n|/n, is positive and C^1 on [0, m) and strictly decreasing there, with v'(λ) < 0 for 0 < λ < m and right derivative -2 E[1/ν] at 0. The hypotheses are the closed propositions CertACovers and CertBCovers that the interval verifications of Lemmas A.1 and A.2 check, over all feasible normalized data; the proof derives the two lemmas from them at the actual law. The two propositions are proved in a companion repository, not in this one.
entries.title: The speed of biased random walk on leafless Bienaymé trees is monotone

entries.abstract: Lean 4 proofs of four lower bounds for Erdős-Rado numbers: k(7,3) ≥ 39, k(8,3) ≥ 47, k(6,4) ≥ 78 and k(3,6) ≥ 71. Here k(n,m) is the least k such that every oriented graph on k vertices has n vertices with no arc between any two of them, or a transitive tournament on m vertices (Erdős Problem #112). Each bound is one explicit oriented graph that avoids both structures: bicirculants on 38 and 46 vertices for k(7,3) and k(8,3), and circulants on 77 and 70 vertices for k(6,4) and k(3,6). Every property of each graph is checked by computations inside Lean's kernel (decide +kernel), with no native_decide, and the proofs use only the axioms propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice. The previous best public lower bounds were k(7,3) ≥ 37, k(8,3) ≥ 46, k(6,4) ≥ 65 and k(3,6) ≥ 68, from circulants in an unrefereed, AI-generated GitHub repository (rsvaultpudgy-create/erdos-112-lower-bounds, 11 November 2026). The four new graphs were first made public in the author's Zenodo record of 20 November 2026 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24390891), which this project formalizes; to the author's knowledge no other proof of these bounds exists, so these are the first Lean proofs of them. Earlier computational work on the problem includes D. Kirtchakov's certified value k(3,4) = 21 and bound k(6,3) ≥ 29 (Zenodo, August 2026). The known upper bounds k(7,3) ≤ 45 and k(8,3) ≤ 59 (Ihringer, Rajendraprasad and Weinert, 2021) are not improved. The results are lower bounds only: none of the four values is determined, and Erdős Problem #112 remains open.
entries.title: Lower bounds for four small Erdős-Rado numbers: k(7,3) ≥ 39, k(8,3) ≥ 47, k(6,4) ≥ 78, k(3,6) ≥ 71 (Erdős Problem #112)

entries.abstract: There exists a simple graph on Fin 100 with no triangle and no independent set of size 18. This is the witness formulation of R(3,18) > 100. The proof checks the adjacency data of the 100-vertex graph published in Zenodo record 24285935. In the complement, a greedy coloring bounds the clique size at each search node and the branches cover all candidates that exceed the color bound. Lean checks the resulting subproblems and their composition using only Lean core and Std.
entries.title: A Lean proof of the Ramsey lower bound R(3,18) >= 101

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof that there are seven points in the Euclidean plane, no three on a line and no four on a circle, whose 21 pairwise distances are all integers. This is the case n = 7 of Erdős Problem 213, which asks whether such sets exist for every n; for n >= 8 the question is open, and seven is the largest size known. The proof checks the integral heptagon of diameter 22270 found by Kreisel and Kurz (2008), using the exact coordinates they give, each of the form (a, b sqrt 2002) with a, b rational. Writing every point this way reduces the three conditions to integer identities: each squared distance, each triangle's cross product and each four-point circle determinant equals an explicit integer times a power of 2227 (and, for the last two, sqrt 2002), and the kernel checks those integers with decide. The geometric half proves that a collinear triple has zero cross product and that four concyclic points have zero circle determinant. The construction is classical and no mathematical priority is claimed. It is the statement erdos_213.variants.KK08 of Formal Conjectures, which marks it research solved.
entries.title: The Kreisel-Kurz heptagon: seven points in the plane, no three on a line, no four on a circle, with integer distances

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, built on Mathlib, of the paper An extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding. Over every field k there is an essentially small k-linear extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding into a triangulated category in any universe, whose countable families of objects lie in extension-closed subcategories with algebraic realizations, and which is hereditary and Krull–Schmidt, has enough injectives and ℵ₁ isomorphism classes of indecomposables with endomorphism ring k, extension spaces of dimension at most one between indecomposables, and morphism spaces of countable dimension (Theorem A). It is the category C(D) attached to an inverse system D of vector spaces with surjective transition maps over an ordinal; C(D) has a triangulated embedding iff every projection lim D → D_i is surjective iff it has an algebraic realization (Theorem B). The library also proves Propositions 2.3, 4.4 and 4.6, Corollary 2.4, Example 4.2, Jech's Aronszajn tree and Bergman's lemma on linearized inverse limits.
entries.title: An extriangulated category with no triangulated embedding

entries.abstract: The binary operator eml(x, y) = exp(x) - ln(y), with the constant 1 and a variable x, generates the elementary functions (Odrzywolek, arXiv:2603.21852). We formalize, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, a computable translation of Richardson expressions (built from rationals, pi, ln 2, x, +, *, sin, exp and |.|) into EML trees evaluated over the complex numbers with the principal logarithm. The translation preserves the value at every real x, including 0 and negative values, and no compiled tree ever applies log to 0 at any real input. Consequently, assuming Richardson's theorem as an explicit hypothesis, deciding whether an EML tree is identically zero on the reals, and deciding whether it has a real root, are both not computable. Both results also hold when log 0 is left undefined or is assigned any fixed value, so they do not depend on a convention for log 0. With the same compiler, three further problems are undecidable under the same hypothesis: whether two EML trees agree at every real x, whether a tree takes a negative real value at some real x, and whether a tree is constant on the reals (using continuity of Richardson expressions). The delicate part is controlling the branch cuts of the complex logarithm: signed arithmetic is carried out through positive quantities, pi and sin are obtained through complex values with imaginary parts kept inside (-pi, pi], and the absolute value is computed as a times the sign of a, where the sign is read off the branch cut of log without ever taking log 0.
entries.title: EML trees: zero-equivalence and root existence are undecidable, assuming Richardson's theorem

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Theorem 1.2 of Lee and Yin, "A necessary and sufficient condition for edge universality of Wigner matrices" (Duke Math. J. 163 (2014), arXiv:1206.2251), for real symmetric Wigner matrices and the largest eigenvalue lambda_N. Let x_12 be an off-diagonal entry. Sufficiency: if s^4 P(|x_12| >= s) -> 0 as s -> infinity (condition (1.4)), then the distribution of N^{2/3}(lambda_N - 2) agrees with that of the GOE up to a shift N^{-delta} and an additive error epsilon_N -> 0 uniform in s (the comparison (4.9)). Necessity: if (1.4) fails, then limsup_N P(lambda_N >= 3) > 0, and N^{2/3}(lambda_N - 2) is not tight and converges in distribution to no probability law. No result of another work is assumed: the local semicircle law, rigidity, the Green function comparison and the edge universality results that the paper cites are proved in the library from Mathlib.
entries.title: A necessary and sufficient condition for edge universality of Wigner matrices

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Parts (ii), (iii), and (iv) of Erdős Problem 1172. Parts (ii) and (iii) are new mathematical results proved in ZFC + GCH (Cardinal.GCH): ω₃ → (ω₂ + ω₁, ω₂ + ω)² and ω₂ → (ω₁^(ω + 2) + 2, ω₁ + 2)², matching Baumgartner, Hajnal, and Todorčević (1993, p. 2) and the 1999 Budapest problem booklet [Va99, 7.87] verbatim, both previously open in the set-theory literature. Part (iv) gives the first formalization of the known relative consistency result (Laver 1982; Foreman-Hajnal 2003) for the ω₁ + ω case posed by Erdős and Hajnal (1974, p. 272): relative to a huge cardinal κ with target θ (IsHugeWithTarget κ θ, Kanamori Theorem 24.8) and ground GCH at and above θ, the first-order theory ZFC + GCH + ω₂ → (ω₁ + ω, ω₁ + ω)² (gchPart4Theory) is syntactically consistent; the stronger simultaneous all-target question ∀ ξ < ω₂, ω₂ → (ξ)²₂ under GCH remains open and is not addressed. For Part (i), erdosproblems.com/1172's cropped-scan binary reconstruction is omitted, and the original un-cropped Baumgartner-Hajnal-Todorčević (1993, p. 2) countable-color question ω₃ → (ω₂ + 2)²_ω under GCH remains open and is not claimed (an unselected remark in Erdos1172/CountableNeighborhoodStep.lean notes that our countable-color neighborhood ideal on ω₃ recovers the known ω₂ + 1 case GCH → ω₃ → (ω₂ + 1)²_ω due to Erdős and Rado, [ErRa56]; [BHT93, Theorem 2.1]).
entries.title: Erdős 1172: GCH ordinal partition relations on ω₂ and ω₃ and huge-cardinal consistency of ω₂ → (ω₁ + ω)²₂

entries.abstract: Consider integer combinations f = sum_z c_z (G_z * h_z) of Dirichlet convolutions in which each core G_z is the Dirichlet power zeta^z (z >= 0) or mu^|z| (z < 0) and each correction h_z vanishes on squarefree integers greater than 1. Target D_k asks that f(q) = p^v u_q (mod p^(v+k)) at every prime q with p not dividing u_q, and that f(n) = 0 (mod p^(v+k)) whenever n has at least two distinct prime factors; summing an f that meets a strong form of D_k (one value at every prime power) gives pi(x) modulo p^k. The development proves that, for every prime p and every k >= 1, the least Z for which some combination with degrees in {-Z..Z} meets D_k is S(p^ceil(k/2)), and with degrees in {1..Z} (no inverse factors) it is S(p^k), where S(m) is the least s with m dividing s! (the Kempner function). As corollaries no combination detects primes modulo p, and the divided target needs a degree divisible by p. It also proves D_3(x) = floor(x^(1/3)) + 3H(x), where H(x) counts triples (a, b, c) with abc <= x, a <= b and a < c, and certifies an algorithm for pi(x) mod 3 through D_3.
entries.title: M2Polymath: the exact degree of divisor-sum identities for the prime-counting function modulo prime powers

entries.abstract: For the rational plane curve parametrization x ↦ ((x-1)/x^n, (x-1)^2/(x-K)^m) with real K>1 and integers n,m at least two, the index of its coordinate field in R(x) is one except at (n,m,K)=(2,4,2), where it is two. In the exceptional case the involution x ↦ x/(x-1) preserves both coordinates.
entries.title: Rational Recovery on a Common Ruler

entries.abstract: Let f be a nonconstant entire function of finite hyper-order outside the positive integers. If f and its derivative share a finite complex value a counting multiplicities, then f' - a = c(f - a) on the complex plane for a nonzero complex constant c.
entries.title: Brück's conjecture

entries.abstract: Lean 4 and Mathlib proofs of three theorems on Serrin's overdetermined problem in epigraphs. Let Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, n ≥ 2, be the epigraph of a continuously differentiable function g on ℝⁿ⁻¹, and let u be positive, twice continuously differentiable in Ω and continuously differentiable up to the boundary, with −Δu = f(u) in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, and outward normal derivative equal to a negative constant on ∂Ω. The reaction f is continuously differentiable on [0, ∞) and satisfies f(s) − s f′(s) ≥ 0 for s > 0. (1) If log(1 + ∫_{Ω∩B_R} u²)/R has liminf zero as R → ∞, then the vertical derivative ∂u/∂xₙ is positive throughout Ω. (2) If moreover f > 0 on (0, 1), f(1) = 0, f′(1) < 0 and u < 1, and n ≤ 8, then g is affine and u depends only on the distance to the hyperplane ∂Ω. (3) Under the assumptions of (2) with n ≥ 9 instead, the same conclusion holds when g has a global linear lower bound or a global linear upper bound. Theorems (2) and (3) are the rigidity theorem of Beuvin and Farina for vertically monotone solutions (arXiv:2502.04812, Theorem 2.1, which builds on work of Wang and Wei), with the monotonicity hypothesis removed by theorem (1), for this class of reactions. Every step is proved in Lean from Mathlib, using only the standard axioms.
entries.title: Serrin epigraph monotonicity and rigidity

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization, in the arithmetic cost model, of fast matrix multiplication and its use in Gaussian elimination. Algorithms are written in a writer monad that charges one unit for every addition, subtraction, negation, multiplication and inversion performed through its primitives; costs are statements about these explicit algorithms, whose definitions are part of the statements. A matrix multiplication algorithm is a counted procedure together with proofs that it computes the product and performs at most M(n) operations on n x n matrices, M monotone. Six theorems are compared: (1) over every ring, Strassen's algorithm on matrices of size 2^k computes the product with exactly 7^k multiplications and 6(7^k - 4^k) additive operations; (2) 2 < log2(7) < 3, and over every ring Strassen's algorithm padded with zeros to the next power of two is a multiplication algorithm with at most 49 n^(log2 7) operations for n >= 1, whose bound satisfies 4 M(2^k) <= M(2^(k+1)) and 1 <= M(1); (3) over a field, for every multiplication algorithm whose bound satisfies these two conditions, block inversion of diag(A, 1) padded to size 2^ceil(log2 n) returns the inverse and the determinant of an n x n matrix A whose leading principal minors are all nonzero, and performs fewer than 5 M(2^ceil(log2 n)) operations (at most 5 C 2^omega n^omega when n >= 1, omega >= 0 and M(m) <= C m^omega for all m >= 1); (4)-(6) for every field K, every multiplication algorithm over K with M(m) <= C m^omega for m >= 1, omega > 2, satisfying the two conditions above, and every plane graph (respectively the square of a plane graph of maximum degree at most D) on n vertices, there is a separator tree covering all vertices such that block elimination along it computes the determinant of every matrix over K whose off-diagonal nonzero entries are edges of that graph, provided the elimination meets only invertible blocks (theorem (6): no such hypothesis for positive definite matrices, on squares of plane graphs, over a field with a partial order and a star structure satisfying IsOrderedRing, PosMulReflectLT and StarRing, such as the real numbers), with at most (5 C 2^omega + 2C + 2)(2T + 1)^omega / (1 - (2/3)^(omega/2 - 1)) n^(omega/2) operations, T = 50000, respectively T = 40 (1062 (D + 1)^2 + 1). Plane graphs are rotation systems of connected Mathlib simple graphs satisfying Euler's formula, so they have at least one edge (faces are cycles of darts, and the one-vertex graph has none). The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Strassen's algorithm, inversion in O(M(n)) and nested dissection with fast matrix multiplication, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: For m ≥ 0 let u_m(n) be the numerator of the sum over k = 1, ..., n of binomial(n,k)^2 binomial(n+k,k)^2 / k^(2m+1). Peter Bala conjectured in OEIS A357513 (2022) that u_m(p-1) ≡ 0 (mod p^4) for all primes p, with finitely many exceptions that depend on m. This project gives a Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of that statement: for every m and every prime p ≥ 2m + 6, p^4 divides u_m(p-1). The proof writes T_k = binomial(p-1,k) binomial(p-1+k,k) as T_k^2 ≡ p^2/k^2 - 2p^3/k^3 (mod p^4), reduces the sum to the harmonic-type sums H(s) = sum of k^(-s) over 1 ≤ k ≤ p-1, shows H(2m+4) ≡ 0 (mod p) with the power sums of the finite field F_p, and shows H(2m+3) ≡ 0 (mod p^2) by pairing k with p - k. The compared theorem is the statement `OeisA357513.general_supercongruence` of the Formal Conjectures repository. The result is not new: Ondrej Kutal proved it in July 2026, with the exact set of exceptional primes and a Lean formalization. The proof here was found independently of Kutal's work and gives only the bound p < 2m + 6 on the exceptional primes.
entries.title: OEIS A357513: u_m(p-1) ≡ 0 (mod p^4) for all primes p ≥ 2m + 6

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of three results of optimal control: the Pontryagin maximum principle and Filippov's theorem, following A. A. Agrachev and Yu. L. Sachkov, Control Theory from the Geometric Viewpoint (Encyclopaedia of Mathematical Sciences 87, Springer, 2004), Chapter 12 and Theorem 10.1, and Noether's theorem for optimal control, following H. J. Sussmann, Symmetries and integrals of motion in optimal control (Banach Center Publications 32, 1995), Theorem 4.1. Control systems q' = f(q, u) live on an open subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space, with measurable controls and trajectories in the sense of Caratheodory.

The maximum principle is proved with free terminal time, an integral cost and mixed boundary conditions (q(0), q(T)) in N, for strong local minimizers, with C^1 data and a compact control set: there are nu <= 0 and a Lipschitz covector curve p, with (nu, p(t)) nonzero for every t, that satisfy the adjoint equation, the maximum condition and the vanishing of the Hamiltonian for almost every t, and the transversality condition. Agrachev and Sachkov leave this case to the reader; their Lemmas 12.1 and 12.2 and Theorems 12.1-12.5 (the geometric maximum principle, free time without cost, and integral costs with fixed, separated and mixed boundary conditions) are proved too. Filippov's theorem: for a continuous control system with compact control set, convex velocity sets and bounded velocities, the attainable sets at time T and up to time T are compact; hence optimal controls exist for integral costs whose extended velocity sets are convex, with fixed or free terminal time. Both results are also proved, by the same argument, for problems posed on part of the space: trajectories confined to a closed set S (the dynamics and the cost need only be continuous, the velocities bounded and the velocity sets convex on S x U), starting in a compact set, with initial and terminal points in a closed relation, and terminal times in a window [T0, T1]. Noether's theorem: if every map of the flow of a C^1 vector field Y is a symmetry of the system that leaves the cost invariant (it may permute the controls), the momentum p(t)(Y(q(t))) is constant along every pair (q, p) that satisfies the adjoint equation and the maximum condition, for any multiplier and any set of control values. Sussmann's Theorem 4.1, for a Lie algebra acting by such symmetries and his biextremals, follows, and so does a maximum principle whose multiplier keeps every such momentum constant.

Everything the proofs use is proved: existence, uniqueness and differentiable dependence of Caratheodory solutions, the variations formula and needle variations, Lebesgue points, measurable selection (Kuratowski-Ryll-Nardzewski), and the flows of C^1 vector fields with their derivative at time 0. Brouwer's fixed-point theorem is taken from the separate Lean package FixedPoint. No axiom beyond Lean's standard three is used.
entries.title: The Pontryagin maximum principle, Filippov's theorem and Noether's theorem for optimal control

entries.abstract: For a prime p and k >= 1, the least L for which the Möbius function is congruent modulo p^k to a sum of zeta^z * E_p(g_z) over the levels z <= L, with zeta^z the Dirichlet powers of zeta, E_p the Frobenius pushforward (E_p g)(j^p) = g(j) and integer valued g_z, is S(p^k) - 1, where S(p^k) is the Kempner value, the least N with p^k dividing N!. The same upper bound holds for the Dirichlet inverse of every f with f(1) a unit, over every commutative ring; over Z and Z_p it is exact as soon as there are n primes q with p not dividing f(q) and p^n >= S(p^k), with no multiplicativity assumed. In the power series rings Z[[x_1, ..., x_n]] and Z_p[[x_1, ..., x_n]] with the lift x_i -> x_i^p, and in the Dirichlet ring over Z and Z_p, the exact level count of every unit is given by a depth-flag formula of Legendre type. The development also proves Conjecture 4 of Kauers, Krattenthaler and Müller for every prime p: the least t-degree of a monic A in Z[z][t] with A(z, Phi_p(z)) congruent to 0 modulo p^gamma, where Phi_p(z) is the sum of z^(p^n), is S(p^gamma).
entries.title: Frobenius: Frobenius congruences for the Möbius function and the exact number of divisor levels

entries.abstract: A formal proof of Iwasawa's classical class-number growth theorem. For an increasing tower of finite cyclic Galois extensions K_n/K of a number field with degrees p^n, the p-adic multiplicity of the class number of K_n equals mu*p^n + lambda*n + nu for all sufficiently large n, with natural mu and lambda and integer nu. The compared statement uses only Mathlib concepts. Its proof constructs the union as a Z_p-extension and discharges the Hilbert class field inputs using the external Nyll class field theory library. The library also contains the cyclotomic specialization. This formalizes a known theorem and makes no claim of a new mathematical result.
entries.title: Formalization of Iwasawa Theory in Lean

entries.abstract: The newform f(z) = η(z)²η(11z)² = q∏(1 − qⁿ)²(1 − q¹¹ⁿ)² = ∑a(n)qⁿ of weight 2 and level 11 (LMFDB 11.2.a.a, the modular form of the elliptic curves of conductor 11) is congruent modulo 5 to the Eisenstein series of its level: a(n) ≡ ∑_{d | n, 11 ∤ d} d (mod 5) for every n ≥ 1, and in particular a(p) ≡ 1 + p (mod 5) for every prime p ≠ 11. It is the weight-2, level-11 analogue of Ramanujan's τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) (mod 691); 5 is the numerator of (11 − 1)/12. Method, as for 691: (1) the lattice L = B ⊕ B with B = (2 1; 1 6), the norm form of x² + xy + 3y² of discriminant −11, is even of rank 4, level dividing 11 and determinant 11², so its theta series θ is a modular form of weight 2 on Γ₀(11) with trivial character (Hecke–Schoeneberg), with integer coefficients r(n) and r(0) = 1; (2) at prime level a weight-2 form minus the Eisenstein multiple with the same constant term at ∞ is a cusp form, so θ = Ẽ + c·f with Ẽ = (E₂(z) − 11E₂(11z))/(−10) = 1 + (12/5)∑σ*(n)qⁿ, because the cusp forms are the multiples of f; (3) comparing coefficients, 5r(n) = 12σ*(n) + (5r(1) − 12)a(n), so 5 divides 12(σ*(n) − a(n)).
entries.title: The Eisenstein congruence modulo 5 for the newform of level 11

entries.abstract: Three commuting square matrices of size n over any field generate a unital subalgebra of dimension at most n. The proof studies the actions on the kernel and cokernel of a nilpotent generator.
entries.title: The Gerstenhaber dimension bound for three commuting matrices over arbitrary fields

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of Chafaï and Fathi, "On cutoff via rigidity for high dimensional curved diffusions" (Comptes Rendus Mathématique 363 (2025) 1103-1121), in the corrected version arXiv:2412.15969v5. The submitted statement surface PalomarChallenge.lean (Comparator configuration comparator-palomar.json) states the theorems and corollaries of the paper (Theorems 1.1, 1.5, 1.7, 1.9, 3.1, 3.6, Corollaries 1.3, 1.4, 1.6): 9 theorems. The repository also contains a larger surface, Challenge.lean with comparator.json (69 theorems: remarks, examples and Section 4 as well). Both are proved with the standard axioms only. Some statements are restricted or amended; every difference with arXiv v5 is listed in fidelity.divergences.
entries.title: Cutoff via rigidity for curved diffusions

entries.abstract: Verification of Theorems 1 and 2 on the stability of Szarek's inequality with best constant, as shown in the source.
entries.title: Stability of Szarek's inequality with best constant

entries.abstract: The four-digit Kaprekar map in base B sends an integer 0 <= x < B^4, written with four base-B digits (leading zeros allowed), to the descending arrangement of its digits minus the ascending arrangement. A cycle is a periodic orbit through an input whose digits are not all equal. Cycles are counted up to cyclic shift, including fixed points of least period one. This formalization uses only Lean 4 core and Std and proves Theorem 1 of R. Galyavin, "Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases" (2026). For B = m*2^n with m odd, n >= 1 and m >= 5, each cycle of the folded map on odd difference pairs lifts to a cycle of the same length. There is one additional cycle of length n+1 if 2^n is 1 modulo m, or one of length 2(n+1) if m = 5 and n is 2 modulo 4. The two conditions are mutually exclusive and the list is exhaustive. For m = 3, odd n gives one cycle of length 3(n+1), and even n gives two cycles of lengths n+1 and 2(n+1). Base two has two fixed points. In base 2^n for odd n >= 3 there are (n-1)/2 cycles of each length n and n+2. For even n >= 2 there are (n-2)/2 cycles of each of those lengths, one of length n/2 and one of length n/2+1. The map is stated directly as digit sorting and subtraction on natural numbers.
entries.title: Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases

entries.abstract: Lean formalizations accompanying twenty numerical linear algebra problem resolutions. They give uniform matrix-product growth and local 1/d-Hölder continuity of the joint spectral radius; two real generators with any prescribed nonnegative polynomial growth exponent; and sharp losses 2^r and 4^r for randomly pivoted Cholesky and LU. They show that concave matrix functions can destroy spectral approximation guarantees and amplify nuclear-norm excess without bound, and give sharp Frobenius transfer bounds with and without semidefinite order. Further results are the random-row adversarial deletion limit and sharp universal deletion constant, a pointwise strict tensor-train bound with unchanged worst-case supremum, and curves with rank savings delayed through any prescribed finite range of tensor powers. Counterexamples concern derivative roots of nonnegative characteristic polynomials, a q-permanent subset inequality, a geometric-mean norm inequality, and weighted log-majorisation. The development also proves the rectangular Rowland-Wu Sinkhorn identity, disconnected quotients of minimal positive semidefinite factors, stable nonsynchronised equilibria on random cubic graphs with high probability, and NP-hardness of exact determinant ranges and solution hulls for regular tridiagonal interval matrices. This repository prepares the proofs for Palomar through a single repository-root Challenge/Solution interface selecting all twenty problem resolutions. Seventeen component environments have recorded Lean 4.35.0 compilation and selected-axiom checks; the combined environment has separate current evidence. Official Palomar and independent NanoDa verification remain pending submission.
entries.title: Numerical Linear Algebra, Explained: Twenty Problem Resolutions

entries.abstract: Hadwiger (Math. Ann. 127, 1954) extended Dehn's invariant to convex polytopes in R^n: for the faces of codimension 2, the sum of their (n-2)-dimensional volume tensored with the dihedral angle modulo rational multiples of pi is kept under dissection. This entry defines that invariant from the set alone, in every finite-dimensional real inner product space: at each point the cone of directions that stay in the set, its lineality space, and, where that space has codimension 2, the angle of the cone in the orthogonal plane; the invariant sums (n-2)-dimensional Hausdorff measure tensored with the angle class, in R tensor_Q (R / Q pi). It proves the bridge: scissors-congruent convex polytopes (pieces are convex polytopes moved by isometries) have the same invariant, in every dimension, also for finite unions of convex polytopes. In R^4 it computes the invariant of the six regular polytopes: zero for the tesseract, the 16-cell, the 24-cell and the 120-cell; for the 5-cell it is A5 tensor arccos(1/4) and for the 600-cell A600 tensor (4 pi / 3 - arccos(1/4)), where A is the area of the ridge points, positive in both; arccos(1/4) is not a rational multiple of pi (Niven's theorem in Mathlib). Hence no similar copy of the 5-cell or of the 600-cell is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the tesseract, the 16-cell, the 24-cell or the 120-cell, and, because the 600-cell's dihedral angle is 4 pi / 3 minus the 5-cell's, their invariants have opposite signs and no similar copy of the 5-cell is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the 600-cell. The non-congruence of the regular simplex and the cube is Hadwiger's (1954, section V); the entry claims no new mathematics, only the formalization. The 600-cell needs the face structure: at every ridge point the two tight facets are neighbours across a triangle; this is proved from exact Z[phi] data (its 600 facet normals, 120 corners and, for every facet, its four corners and four neighbours) checked by kernel evaluation, with a barycentric argument on the facet. Not formalized: Jessen's converse in R^4 (equal volume and equal invariant imply scissors congruence), Hadwiger's other invariants in higher dimensions, and the identification of the set invariant with the face sum for every convex polytope (the six polytopes are computed directly). The library reuses the Dehn Canon development (registered PALOMAR-2026-11-20-000003) for convex polytopes, cones, wedge angles, cuts and dissections. Audience: researchers on scissors congruence, valuations on polytopes and regular polytopes, and Mathlib contributors.
entries.title: The Dehn–Hadwiger invariant in four dimensions

entries.abstract: A Lean formalization of the sharp upper tail bound for sums of independent identically distributed nonnegative random variables, including all maximizing laws and boundary cases, and the exact Erdős matching bound with its equality classification for every fixed uniformity k >= 3 and all sufficiently large matching parameters, uniformly over n >= k(s+1).
entries.title: Sharp i.i.d. tail probabilities and large hypergraph matchings

entries.abstract: For the ideal two-step Boschi–Hardy ladder with three binary settings per observer and five exact zeros, the fixed-state maximum for four positive Schmidt coefficients is the best of three disjoint pairings. The proof covers arbitrary complex binary effects and gives attaining projective measurements. Equality at the two-qubit plastic-constant value holds exactly when both pairs have smaller-to-larger ratio ρ⁻². A finite mixture of pure components through Schmidt rank four obeys the same ceiling. Every full-rank pure qutrit is strictly below it. A pure state with twelve distinct positive Schmidt weights attains the value through six orthogonal qubit sectors.
entries.title: The Two-Step Hardy Ladder in Higher Dimensions

entries.abstract: The four-digit Kaprekar map in base B sends an integer 0 <= x < B^4, written with four base-B digits (leading zeros allowed), to the descending arrangement of its digits minus the ascending arrangement. A cycle is a periodic orbit through an input whose digits are not all equal. Cycles are counted up to cyclic shift, including fixed points of least period one. This formalization uses only Lean 4 core and Std and proves that an even base B >= 2 has exactly one cycle if and only if B = 3*2^(2k+1) or B = 5*2^(2k+1) for some k >= 0, or B = 7*2^n with n >= 1 and n not divisible by 3. In these three families the unique cycle has length 6(k+1), 1 and 3, respectively; base ten is 5*2^1, with the fixed point 6174. This is Corollary 2 of R. Galyavin, "Cycles of the four-digit Kaprekar map in even bases" (2026). It proves the pattern that Chen, Ono, Schwartz and Thakur recorded from numerical evidence (J. Integer Seq. 29 (2026), Remark 28). The map is stated directly as digit sorting and subtraction on natural numbers. The underlying Lean development also proves the paper's Theorem 1, the classification of all cycles in every even base m*2^n; that classification is not part of the statement compared here.
entries.title: Even bases with exactly one four-digit Kaprekar cycle

entries.abstract: For every positive real epsilon, there is a positive constant C such that log c is at most C times rad(abc) to the power epsilon whenever a and b are positive coprime integers and a + b = c. The radical is the product of the distinct prime factors. This is an upper bound for log c. The abc conjecture itself remains open.
entries.title: A subexponential upper bound for log c in the abc conjecture

entries.abstract: For every positive real epsilon, there is a positive constant C such that log c is at most C times rad(abc) to the power 2/9 + epsilon whenever a and b are positive coprime integers and a + b = c. The radical is the product of the distinct prime factors. This is an upper bound for log c. The abc conjecture itself remains open.
entries.title: An upper bound for log c in the abc conjecture with exponent 2/9

entries.abstract:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the stable manifold theorem for maps, in graph form. Let f be of class C^n, 1 <= n <= infinity, on a neighborhood of a fixed point p of a finite-dimensional real normed space E, with derivative A = Df(p) invertible and hyperbolic (no complex eigenvalue of modulus 1), and let E_s and E_u be the stable and unstable subspaces of A. Then there are a neighborhood N of p and maps h_s : E_s -> E_u and h_u : E_u -> E_s, of class C^n and vanishing with their derivatives at 0, such that for every neighborhood U of p inside N, the local stable set of f in U (the points whose forward orbit stays in U and tends to p) is the graph {p + x + h_s(x)} of h_s over a neighborhood of 0 in E_s, and the local unstable set (the points with a backward orbit in U tending to p) is the graph {p + y + h_u(y)} of h_u over a neighborhood of 0 in E_u. Inside a small neighborhood of p the convergence is automatic: the local stable set in U is the set of points whose forward orbit stays in U, and the local unstable set the set of points with a backward orbit in U. The stable side is also proved without invertibility, with one h_s for every neighborhood inside a small ball around p. Also proved: the hyperbolic splitting E = E_s (+) E_u for a hyperbolic linear map of a finite-dimensional real space, with E_s and E_u the kernels of the factors of the characteristic polynomial with roots inside and outside the unit circle.

The proof is Perron's method on the Banach space of bounded sequences. The splitting comes from a factorization of the characteristic polynomial and Gelfand's formula, and gives an exponential dichotomy. After a cut-off by a bump function, f is a globally small Lipschitz perturbation F of A near p; the bounded forward orbits of F are the fixed points of a contraction built from the Lyapunov-Perron operator, and form the graph of a Lipschitz map over E_s. Smoothness of every order comes at once, without the fiber contraction theorem: the composition operator x -> phi o x is C^n on bounded sequences when phi is, and the inverse function theorem on the space of bounded sequences makes the graph C^n. The unstable side is the stable side of the local inverse of f. No earlier formal proof of the theorem for maps was found; a concurrent Lean 4 development (TauCeti) proves stable and unstable manifolds for equilibria of vector fields.
entries.title: The stable manifold theorem for a hyperbolic fixed point of a smooth map, with the hyperbolic splitting

entries.abstract: Let T be a tempered distribution on the real line with value-only atomic records for T and its Fourier transform on locally finite carriers. If the point count on either ray of the physical carrier is bounded by C times the radius along arbitrarily large radii, a nonzero finite real-frequency exponential polynomial annihilates T. The opposite carrier only needs to be locally finite for this implication. When the counted carrier is the actual support and the centred count of the opposite carrier has zero quadratic lower density, both records are finite sums of translated and modulated lattice Dirac combs. The latter conclusion also holds with the Fourier record as the counted actual support. The radii witnessing lower density may be sparse.
entries.title: Annihilation and finite-comb classification from finite lower density on one ray

entries.abstract: If a product of two monic real polynomials with nonnegative coefficients is binary and one factor has exactly three nonzero coefficients, both factors are binary. Two independent finitely supported integer laws are each uniform on their support when their sum is uniform on its support and one law has exactly three support points. This formalization uses Fourier series.
entries.title: The Unfair 0–1 Polynomial Conjecture for Trinomial Factors

entries.abstract: For every finite index type n, the integral symplectic group Sp(2n, ℤ) is generated by the matrix J = (0 −1; 1 0), the translations (1 S; 0 1) with S symmetric, and the matrices (U 0; 0 Vᵀ) with UV = VU = 1 (the image of GL(n, ℤ)). The proof does not induct on n. It inducts on a set s of indices: every symplectic matrix that fixes the basis vectors e_j, j ∈ s, of the first half of ℤⁿ ⊕ ℤⁿ lies in the generated subgroup. In the step, the column M e_i = (a, c) is moved to e_i by elements that fix the e_j: first Euclid's algorithm in each coordinate k ∉ s makes c = 0, using (1 tE_kk; 0 1) and its conjugate by J; then a descent on the sum of |a_k| over k ∉ s, by units of M_n(ℤ) of the form 1 + c·e_lᵀ, reduces a to e_i, the last nonzero entry being ±1 because a row of the inverse matrix gives a Bezout relation.
entries.title: Generators of the integral symplectic group Sp(2n, ℤ)

entries.abstract: Verification of the asymptotic count of Boolean threshold functions and the linear dependence probability of independent uniform sign vectors.
entries.title: BooleanThreshold

entries.abstract: Let Λ be a locally finite subset of the real line with a uniform bound on the number of points in each integer unit cell. The whole complex Meyer space of tempered distributions T with value-only atomic physical and Fourier records on Λ has finite dimension. Its dimension equals the attained maximum of nullities over finite unions L of translated positive-step full lattices for which L ∖ Λ is finite. For each L, the original physical and Fourier coefficients must both vanish at every missing site. In finite lattice residue coordinates, subtracting the joint rank of these rows from the sum of the cyclotomic block nullities gives the envelope nullity. One such envelope realizes the whole space. With separate relatively separated carriers both members of the Fourier pair are finite sums of translated and modulated lattice Dirac combs. The separately stated one-record H6 theorem only bounds the physical carrier. The active spectral module is finitely generated, and a single nonzero exponential polynomial with frequencies in that module annihilates every member of the fixed-carrier space.
entries.title: Finite-comb and finite-hole classification for relatively separated carriers

entries.abstract: An integral unit constructed from the roots of X⁴−X−1 gives a two-qubit diagonal phase gate whose output on the plus product state has concurrence 0.99813134 rounded to eight decimal places. One use entangles a normalized pure product exactly when both qubits have nonzero amplitudes on both basis states. The maximum occurs exactly when both qubits have equal basis probabilities. Among irreducible trace-zero monic integer quartics with two real roots and a complex conjugate pair, require both the generating root and the three squared complementary-pair sums to be algebraic units. For this fixed embedding assignment, phase rule and one use, the joint maximum over all normalized pure product inputs and all eligible polynomial presentations is reached at four polynomials: X⁴±X−1 and X⁴−2X²±X+1. They present the same field by the generators ±Q and ±Q². All other eligible polynomials have squared concurrence at most 307/356, for coefficients of any height.
entries.title: When a Gate from X⁴−X−1 Entangles Two Qubits

entries.abstract: Formalization of the paper "On the cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations" by D. Chafaï, M. Fathi and N. Simonov. For the Fokker–Planck version of the fast diffusion / porous medium equation in ℝᵈ started from a Dirac mass, whose solution is an explicit rescaled Barenblatt profile, the quadratic Wasserstein distance, the Tsallis-type relative entropy and the Fisher information to equilibrium, maximized over initial points in a ball of radius r√d, exhibit a cutoff phenomenon as d → ∞: they jump from +∞ to 0 at the critical time max(1,α)/2 · log d for a fixed self-similarity exponent α ≠ 1/2, and at 1/2 · log d for a fixed exponent m > 1. The formalization also covers the Wasserstein distance between a measure and its image under an affine map with positive semidefinite linear part, the exact Gamma-function formulas for the moments and Lᵐ norms of the full-space and compactly supported Barenblatt profiles and their high-dimensional asymptotics, the normalization of the Barenblatt profile, and the fact that the explicit solution solves the equation.
entries.title: Cutoff phenomenon for fast diffusion and porous medium equations

entries.abstract: A complete formalisation, in Lean 4 with Mathlib, of the Erdős–Kac theorem: the number of distinct prime factors ω(n), centred by log log N and scaled by sqrt(log log N), satisfies a central limit theorem on {1, …, N}. The proof goes through Mertens' second theorem and a truncated sieve whose moments are compared with an independent-prime model. Moment comparison is carried over to characteristic functions by a Taylor truncation of exp(iτs), whose remainder is controlled by a uniform even-moment bound; the model characteristic function converges to the Gaussian, and Lévy's continuity theorem finishes.
entries.title: Erdős–Kac theorem

entries.abstract: Let L be an even unimodular lattice of rank 2k and n a finite index type. The theta series Θ_L(Z) = ∑_{x ∈ Lⁿ} exp(πi tr(G(x)Z)), G(x) the Gram matrix of the tuple x, converges absolutely when Im Z is positive definite, is holomorphic in the entries of Z, is bounded on each region Im Z ≥ c·1, and satisfies Θ_L((AZ + B)(CZ + D)⁻¹) = det(CZ + D)^k Θ_L(Z) for every (A B; C D) in Sp(2n, ℤ) and every Z in the Siegel upper half-space. So Θ_L is a Siegel modular form of degree n and weight k. The transformation law is proved on three kinds of generator. Translations Z ↦ Z + S and the maps Z ↦ UZUᵀ are reindexings of the sum. The inversion Z ↦ −Z⁻¹ is reduced to the inversion formula for a theta series in one variable: for Z = τ·Y with Y real positive definite, Θ_L(Z) is the one-variable theta series of the lattice Lⁿ twisted by a square root of Y, to which TauCeti's inversion formula (Poisson summation) applies; the identity theorem along the path s ↦ s·Re Z + i·Im Z then gives all of the Siegel upper half-space. Finally Sp(2n, ℤ) is generated by the inversion, the translations and the image of GL(n, ℤ).
entries.title: The theta series of an even unimodular lattice is a Siegel modular form

entries.abstract: A rhombic monohedral polyhedron of spherical type (surface homeomorphic to a sphere, adjacent faces not coplanar) with exactly 30 faces, all of them congruent rhombi whose diagonals are in the golden ratio, in which every zone has exactly 10 faces, and whose translates by a lattice tile space face to face. This gives an example for k = 10 for the question of B. Grunbaum (Math. Intelligencer 32(4), 2010): "Given an even integer k >= 4, is there a rhombic monohedral parallelohedron such that every zone has exactly k faces?", where he wrote that "no information is available for any k >= 10". The witness is DICTO's Grunbaum-Escher Triacontahedron GET B: the rhombic triacontahedron less four oblate golden rhombohedra, a union of 16 golden rhombohedra (its exact model also has 32 vertices and 60 edges; these counts are properties of the witness, checked in the model, not part of the theorem). Two calibration theorems check that the zone definition gives 4 for the cube and 6 for the rhombic dodecahedron. Earlier solids of the same family (the rhombic triacontahedron with four corners indented) were shown on the web as space-fillers, without proof, without zone sizes and without reference to Grunbaum's question: by D. Hall (Sketchfab, 2016; the same solid as G. Inchbald's dimpled rhombic triacontahedron, by 2023) and by J. Kostick (vZome, 2022), whose concavo-convex triacon array shows GET A, a sibling of GET B. So this entry does not claim the first example for k = 10. GET B itself was not found in the sources checked. Since GET B is an indentation of the triacontahedron and is proved here to be a parallelohedron, it is also a counterexample to Grunbaum's tentative remark (same paper) that "none of the other isozonohedra obtainable by indentation of F or T seem to be parallelohedra". The proof checks exact data in Z[phi] by kernel evaluation (zones, congruence, separating normals, contacts, face matching, cone separation from an interior point) and derives the tiling from volume = covolume with Mathlib's fundamental domains. The entry is meant for researchers on parallelohedra and space-filling polyhedra (nonconvex parallelohedra, Venkov-McMullen belt theory) and on golden-rhombohedron polyhedra.
entries.title: Grünbaum's zone question at k = 10

entries.abstract: A clearinghouse observes a market with n firms and n+1 workers and can choose any stable assignment. Both sides draw independent rate-one exponential utilities for every firm-worker pair. Changing partners costs log(n)/(6 sqrt(n)). Write δ = 1/400000. As n grows, with probability tending to one, every stable assignment gives the matched workers a mean partner rank greater than n^(1/2+δ) and a mean utility less than (1/2−δ) log(n). Rank one is best. Consequently, even a clearinghouse that chooses separately for each objective cannot deliver mean partner ranks at the square-root benchmark on both sides, or mean utilities at the half-log benchmark on both sides. A working paper on these results is forthcoming.
entries.title: One extra worker rules out the square-root welfare compromise

entries.abstract: For n = 1, …, 8: the least radius of a closed disk holding n unit squares with disjoint interiors, each placed and rotated freely, and every packing that attains it. The radii are √2/2, √5/2, 5√17/16, √2, √(5/2), √q₆ ≈ 1.68854, √13/2 and R₈ ≈ 1.97877, where q₆ is a quartic irrational and R₈ the least radius of a disk about the origin holding five corners with prescribed gaps between them. Up to rotation about the disk centre and relabelling, the optimal packing is unique for n ≤ 6: the square, the 2 × 1 rectangle, the T, the 2 × 2 block, the plus, and for six squares a central square with four neighbours, two of them pushed along its sides, and a sixth square turned by π/4 between those two. For n = 7 the optimal packings form a three-parameter family: two columns of two squares and, between them, a column of three whose heights vary independently, at least 1 apart and within √3 − 1/2 of the disk centre. For n = 8 they form a five-parameter family, with its reflections: five squares have a corner on the circle, two slide, and the central square moves and turns. The proofs for three to six squares bound the arcs the squares occupy on a small circle about the disk centre. For six squares this finds the square that contains the disk centre; five fixed points label the others, and a weighted sum of separating inequalities, with estimates uniform in the angles of the squares, forces the optimal radius. For seven squares, each square avoiding the disk centre gets a direction from it, and in the optimal disk two disjoint such squares get directions at least π/3 apart. For eight squares a central square is found, checked pair, affine and owner tables capture the frames of the seven exterior squares near the stationary configuration, and a completion of squares with the weights of the stationary packing forces the optimal radius. Lean verifies the table bounds and their coverage. The public radius and optimal family retain their geometric five-corner description, proved equivalent to the stationary description used by the tables. The table-free case analysis is deprecated and is absent from the active library. We found no earlier proof for five, six, seven or eight squares, and no exact one for three, where a computer-assisted enclosure of the radius and the optimal arrangements was known. Four squares, uniqueness included, were settled by hand in 2026, by the same idea as here.
entries.title: Optimal packings of one to eight unit squares in a disk

entries.abstract: We prove the Lennon–Pittel conjecture for balanced stable marriage with independent, uniform strict preferences. Let S_n count the stable complete matchings between two sides of size n. For every positive nonincreasing sequence epsilon_n tending to zero, the probability that S_n is at least epsilon_n times its expectation tends to one. This gives a lower-tail estimate at the scale of Pittel's first-moment asymptotic. An accompanying working paper is in preparation.
entries.title: The Lennon–Pittel conjecture on random stable matchings

entries.abstract: Nine isosceles triangles with a common axis in a circle of diameter 1 that meet Huet's conditions in Chiodo's form (the two great triangles inscribed, seven apexes on bases, the 18 marmas and the 6 corner touches), Kulaichev's four conditions (a)-(d) and the admissibility of DICTO's paper #103 (Theorem 1) form exactly one figure (identified with the yantra of #103 Theorem 10 through the slope interval). Its slope w7/b7 is proved to lie in an interval of width 2^-21, [0.7504382776..., 0.7504387544...]; #103 gives the slope as 0.7504385160222140244..., a value computed outside Lean that lies in this interval. This settles Kulaichev's 1984 uniqueness question for admissible (well-formed) figures. The proof combines a kernel-checked branch-and-bound interval certificate (64,613 boxes in 10 charts, with proved monotone-split and slope enclosures), a Krawczyk box (uniqueness by a contraction, existence by Banach's fixed-point theorem), the forced construction from the geometry, and a verified sparse-polynomial normaliser for the identities between them. Not formalised: DICTO's study (outside Lean) finds one other real solution of the same equations, at w7/b7 = 0.66866..., which is not admissible (bases out of order, two negative half-widths), so it is not a yantra. Audiences: the history of mathematics (Kulaichev's question in the Indian Journal of History of Science, called still open in 2021), sacred geometry (the construction of the Sri Yantra), and computer-assisted proof in geometry (a certified interval computation checked by Lean's kernel).
entries.title: Kulaichev's Sri Yantra is unique

entries.abstract: A self-contained, zero-Mathlib Lean 4 formalization of the Combinatorial Four Color Theorem: every finite, complete, Euler-planar, bridgeless orientable combinatorial map (involutive hypermap, `e^2 = id`, `e ∘ n ∘ f = id`) admits a proper 4-coloring of its faces (`Solution.four_color_theorem`). Follows the published mathematics of Robertson, Sanders, Seymour, and Thomas (1996/1997) and Gonthier's hypermap framework (2008), verifying all 633 unavoidable configurations (249 D-reducible and 384 C-reducible) and all 5 cartwheel discharging trees directly inside the Lean kernel without `native_decide`.
entries.title: The Combinatorial Four Color Theorem in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Every integer polynomial with all coefficients odd that differs from both signs of its reverse has multiplicative Mahler measure at least (1 + √5)/2. The polynomial x² − x − 1 meets all these hypotheses and attains the bound.
entries.title: The Golden Ratio as the Sharp Mahler Bound for Nonreciprocal Polynomials with Odd Coefficients

entries.abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of an article on Davison's mosaic spaces and three questions recorded by Lavallee (1964). Formalized: every theorem, lemma, proposition and corollary of Sections 2, 4, 6 and 7 and the classical facts they use (abstract Definition 2.1 and its equivalence with the intrinsic definition; the arc theorem; compact locally connected metrizable spaces are locally path connected; Proposition 2.10 on path-determined spaces), the space G (Tychonoff, locally arcwise connected, not a quasi-curve space), the cone construction, boundary bumping (Lemma 5.2), and the answers to all three questions: Q3 by G, Q2 and Q1a/Q1b by the cone over G. Not formalized (examples, excluded by the author's request): Section 3 and the Appendix (the space E(K)), van Douwen's space in Section 5, Example 7.3 (cZ) and the strictness claims of Theorem 7.4 that use them; also the Hahn-Mazurkiewicz theorem, which no formalized result needs.
entries.title: Mosaic spaces generated by continua and by Peano continua

entries.abstract: Normalized Latin systems of every order m at least five have three-sunlet image dimension 5m-4 in every characteristic, including the original finite abelian-group coordinates. Two transitive derangement families give the stated dimension 3m+2c-2. Complex generic fibers have unique unordered toric decomposition, normalized degree twice the square of the loop abelianization order, and the character-wreath Galois group. The model is rational over Q. Prime nonassociative loops give precisely two normalized general preimages; cyclic models of every order at least six admit rational reconstruction from the literal 8m-12 retained coordinates. Orbit and inverse-stable partition identifications have the complete dimension classification, which yields the full binary level-one network formula including triangles and two leaves.
entries.title: Dimension and identifiability of three-sunlet models

entries.abstract: Principal path construction and simultaneous sharp bounds; exact 3-tree, clique-book, multipartite and lattice classifications. It also constructs, for every n ≥ 10, K5-free graphs of treewidth four with 3n − 5 edges supporting full-dimensional lattice indecomposable polytopal summands; no proper edge-subgraph supports a full-dimensional indecomposable polytopal weak summand.
entries.title: Sharp bounds for indecomposable graphical-zonotope summands: main

entries.abstract:
The Heilbronn number H_n of the unit square is the largest possible least area of a triangle with vertices at three of n points in the closed unit square. This entry proves H₉ = (9√65 − 55)/320 ≈ 0.0548760, and that it is attained only by the configuration of Comellas and Yebra (2002), with two points on each side of the square and one inside, up to the eight symmetries of the square and relabelling.

The proof normalizes a maximizing configuration by affine maps into five families, by the corners of the square it occupies, and excludes or classifies each family by geometric case analysis, sharp inequalities in the chamber of eleven tight triangles, strict local optimality, and polynomial certificates checked by Lean's kernel, about 434,000 weighted terms in all. We found no exact proof of H₉ before this one: a branch and bound had bounded it in an interval, and mixed-integer optimization had found it within solver tolerances (a preprint that claimed a proof in March 2026 withdrew the claim). The repository treats each number of points as a separate entry; nine points is the first.
entries.title: Heilbronn's triangle problem in the unit square: nine points

entries.abstract: The principal results of the included paper characterize volume-polynomial realizability. In dimension d at least three the n-body coefficient locus is semialgebraic exactly for n at most two; the entry includes the polytope clause, forced nonsemialgebraic shapes, and the countable rational quadratic characterization with strict separation, finite certificates, rejection termination and rational polytope reconstruction.
entries.title: Volume polynomials and the Heine–Shephard problem

entries.abstract: The principal results and substantive corollaries of the included paper on coordinate projection areas: rank-three nonapproximation despite realizable four-coordinate restrictions, compatibility of boundary quartets, escape-cone and closure identities, strict realization by centrally symmetric polytopes with the actual vertex bound, weighted obstructions, open nonrealizable families, and the nonnegative rank-at-most-three classification.
entries.title: Compatibility and realization of coordinate projection areas

entries.abstract: Dehn's answer to Hilbert's third problem, with the Dehn invariant defined from the solid as a set of points in 3-space rather than from a list of edges. For a set P, the invariant dehnSet P in R (x)_Q (R/Q pi) adds, over the angle classes theta, the length (1-dimensional Hausdorff measure) of the points of P whose cone of directions has a line as its lineality space and the angle class theta there, the angle being 2 pi times the area of the cone in the unit disc across that line divided by the area of the disc. Proved: (1) Hilbert's problem in his words: two tetrahedra on one and the same base triangle, with apexes at the same distance 1 from its plane and volume 1/6, that are neither scissors congruent nor equicomplementable (pieces: convex polytopes moved by isometries); (2) for every convex polytope with interior points, dehnSet P equals the classical sum over its edges of length (x) dihedral angle, with edges, facets and dihedral angles also defined from the set (Dehn's invariant in Jessen's tensor form); (3) the bridge: scissors-congruent convex polytopes have the same invariant, in every 3-dimensional real inner product space, and for finite unions of convex polytopes the total over the pieces does not depend on the dissection and is kept by scissors congruence; (4) Dehn's theorem: no similar copy of the regular tetrahedron is scissors congruent to a similar copy of the cube. The theorem is classical (Dehn 1901) and already formalized in Lean in FormalBook's chapter 10, in an abstract model of edges and angles; what is added here is the set-defined invariant, the proved bridge from geometric dissections, its agreement with the edge sum, and Hilbert's statement for tetrahedra as point sets. The entry is meant for researchers in formalized geometry and in scissors congruence: since the invariant and the bridge are stated for sets and for every dissection into convex polytopes, they can serve as a base in Lean for Sydler's converse, Jessen's work in four dimensions and a theory of valuations in Mathlib; none of these is attempted here.
entries.title: The Dehn Canon: Hilbert's Third Problem, Machine-Checked

entries.abstract: In every degree, an integer polynomial with nonzero constant coefficient whose reverse differs from both it and its negative has multiplicative Mahler measure at least the plastic number. The cubic x³ − x − 1 attains the bound. In the compositum of its root and a root of x⁴ − x − 1, the least Mahler measure of an algebraic integer other than 0 and ±1 equals the plastic number. Each element uses its own minimal polynomial over ℤ. We also deduce Siegel’s theorem that the plastic number is the smallest Pisot number.
entries.title: Smyth’s Theorem in Lean — The Plastic Number ρ as a Sharp Lower Bound for Mahler Measure

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of maximum flows and shortest paths. Plane graphs are combinatorial maps (darts with a reversal, a tail vertex, a face and a next dart along the face boundary) whose graph and dual are connected and which satisfy Euler's formula V + F = D/2 + 2. The machine statements are about one explicit word RAM (unit cost per instruction, natural registers and memory cells bounded by a word bound W along the run) and fixed encodings of the inputs as lists of natural numbers; each asserts one fixed program for all inputs. Six theorems are compared: (1) the max-flow min-cut theorem for a network with nonnegative integer capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks: some flow and some cut have equal value and capacity, so the flow is maximum and the cut minimum; (2) the theorem of Miller and Naor: on a plane map, given an antisymmetric g with net outflow b at every vertex, a b-flow within the capacities u exists if and only if the dual graph with lengths u - g has a feasible potential; (3) a program decides, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map with V vertices, F faces and S darts, natural capacities, supplies and demands, whether a feasible flow exists, within 26 (S + 2)(V + F + 2) steps; (4) a program prints, for each vertex of a digraph with n vertices, m arcs and natural lengths, its distance from a source capped at a given value INF (so INF for unreachable vertices), within (n + m + 1)(36 floor(log2 n) + 143) steps; (5) a program prints the size of a maximum matching of a bipartite graph with n vertices and m arcs within 80 (n + 1)(n + m + 1) steps; (6) there are a program and constants c and k such that, for every well-formed encoding of a plane map (loops allowed) with n darts, K vertices, natural capacities and disjoint sets of sources and sinks, and every word bound W >= c (7 s)^k, where s is n + K plus the total capacity plus 2, the program prints a maximum flow from the sources to the sinks, as a table of flow values together with a valid index into it for every dart, within c (n + K + 1)(floor(log2 n) + 1)^3 steps; this is the algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
entries.title: Flows and shortest paths in plane graphs, with machine programs including the maximum-flow algorithm of Borradaile, Klein, Mozes, Nussbaum and Wulff-Nilsen, in Lean 4

entries.abstract: Lean 4 formalization of the following power-type loss in the local  Mizohata–Takeuchi estimate. For each $0<\beta\le 1$, there is an exponent $\alpha_\beta>0$ such that, in every dimension $d\ge 1$, each $C^{2,\beta}$ hypersurface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point satisfies $\mathcal{C}_\Sigma(R)\ge c_\Sigma R^{\alpha_\beta}$ for all $R\ge R_\Sigma$. Here $\mathcal{C}_\Sigma(R)$ is the local Mizohata–Takeuchi constant, and the positive constant $c_\Sigma$ and threshold $R_\Sigma$ may depend on $\Sigma$.
entries.title: Power loss for the local Mizohata–Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces

entries.abstract: The equality count for the functions f and F of Erdős Problem 878 is asymptotic to an explicit sum of logarithmic integrals indexed by the cofactor of the largest prime. Finite polynomial tests determine the sets of integration. The argument controls the discarded integers and sums a quantitative prime number theorem over the resulting intervals.
entries.title: An asymptotic formula for the equality count in Erdős Problem 878(iv)

entries.abstract: Let f(n) be the sum over prime divisors p of n of the greatest power of p at most n. The weighted sum of f(n)/n over 1 ≤ n < x is asymptotic to an explicit sum over primes p ≤ (log x)^2. Each prime contributes a term depending on the remainder of log x modulo log p. The proof combines a finite harmonic-sum estimate with a uniform short-interval prime bound.
entries.title: An asymptotic equivalent for the harmonic sum in Erdős Problem 878(v)

entries.abstract: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of the paper "BKT asymptotics for the quenched free energy of hierarchical pinning" (Hexagon preprint 2611.00654v1), except the Gaussian example of its introduction. For B > 2, a disorder W > 0 with E W = 1 and a field h, the partition functions on the diamond hierarchical lattice satisfy R_0 = e^h W and R_{n+1} = (R_n R_n' + B - 1) / B with independent copies; the free energy is F(h) = lim 2^{-n} E log R_n(h) and h_c = sup {h : F(h) = 0}. The main theorem states that if h_c exceeds the annealed critical point h_a = log(B - 1), then with theta = log 2 / log B, a = log B and Pi_n = prod_{j<n} E R_j(h_c)^theta, the residues l_3 = lim E[R_n^theta (log R_n - a)^3] / Pi_n and kappa = lim d/dh E[R_n(h)^theta (log R_n(h) - a)] at h_c, divided by Pi_n, exist and are positive, Pi_n ~ 3 a^3 n^2 / (2 l_3), and sqrt(u) log F(h_c + u) -> -pi log 2 / sqrt(gamma) as u decreases to 0, with gamma = 3 a^2 kappa / (2 l_3): the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless law with explicit constant. All 24 numbered results of the paper are proved, including the basic bounds, critical moments, return to one, the critical product, the field response, the scaling limit and its identification with an explicit profile, continuation before the pole, and the upper and lower free-energy bounds through a hard integer-valued recursion. Three routine identities of Section 1 are used but not exported as standalone declarations.
entries.title: BKT asymptotics for the quenched free energy of hierarchical pinning

entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 2 of J. Brüdern and A. Perelli, Goldbach numbers in sparse sequences, Ann. Inst. Fourier 48, 1998, pages 353 to 378, stated on page 354 and proved in section 8 of the paper. The result is conditional on Theorem 1 of A. A. Karacuba 1973, as cited in the paper's Lemma 10 on pages 370 and 371, which is taken as the explicit hypothesis Lemma10DQ5 and never as an axiom. Let F of x be exp of log x to the power gamma, with 1 < gamma < 3/2. Theorem 2 says that for 0 < c < 1 and 0 < C < gamma - 1 there are kappa > 0 and a constant B such that, for every integer N >= 1 and every real alpha with F of 2N to the power -c <= |alpha| <= F of N to the power C, the exponential sum of e of alpha F of n over N <= n <= 2N has absolute value at most B N exp of -kappa times log N to the power 3 - 2 gamma. The Lean proves the steps of section 8 from Lemma 10: the derivative formulas of Lemmas 11 and 12 for the polynomials Q and q, the bounds of Lemmas 13 to 16 on the derivatives of F, the choice of the parameters, and the application of Lemma 10. Karacuba's theorem itself is not proved here. Binary Goldbach and the paper's Theorem 1 on Goldbach numbers near F of n are not claimed. AI agents wrote the Lean code, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
entries.title: Goldbach numbers in sparse sequences: Theorem 2 on exponential sums

entries.abstract: Let Rₙ(t) be the resultant in x of x² − x − 1 and tⁿ − txⁿ⁻¹ − xⁿ. For every n ≥ 3, we compute Rₙ(t) explicitly in ℤ[t], prove that its remainder modulo t² − t − 1 is (−F₂ₙ + (−1)ⁿ⁺¹)t − F₂ₙ₋₁, and identify the algebra norm of its residue in ℤ[φ] as (−1)ⁿ⁺¹L₂ₙ₋₁. The absolute norm is at least 11, with equality exactly when n = 3. This formalizes Stephanie Alexander’s Theorem 2 for the product resultant and derives the sharp minimum.
entries.title: The Fibonacci remainder and Lucas norm of the product resultant for xⁿ − x − 1

entries.abstract: A machine-checked proof that there is a bounded operator on l1(N, C) with no closed invariant subspace other than 0 and the whole space. This is Read's 1985 counterexample to the invariant subspace problem on l1, following Wieslaw Sliwa's explicit version of Read's operator (Rocky Mountain J. Math. 40, 2010), which replaces "sufficiently rapidly increasing" sequences by concrete growth conditions and proves every lemma. Its audience is operator theory and the geometry of Banach spaces. It is the statement Invariant_subspace_problem_l1 of Formal Conjectures (InvariantSubspaceProblem.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The operator is multiplication by x in a basis of the polynomials built from a fast-growing integer sequence; the proof shows that the vector 1 can be approximated by p(T)e for every nonzero e, so no nonzero closed invariant subspace can be proper. The open case of a separable Hilbert space is not addressed.
entries.title: Read's theorem: a bounded operator on l1 with no nontrivial closed invariant subspace

entries.abstract: The first newform of weight 2 with trivial character, the one attached to the elliptic curves of conductor 11, is constructed and characterised completely, in one statement that uses only Mathlib definitions. f(z) = η(z)²η(11z)² = q∏(1 − qⁿ)²(1 − q¹¹ⁿ)² (LMFDB 11.2.a.a) is a cusp form of weight 2 for Γ₀(11) with integer coefficients a(n), a(1) = 1, a(2) = −2. It spans the cusp forms of weight 2 for Γ₀(11); a modular form of that weight and level agreeing with it up to q² (the Sturm bound) equals it; and its coefficients satisfy the Hecke relations a(m)a(n) = ∑_{d | (m,n), 11 ∤ d} d·a(mn/d²), hence multiplicativity and the prime-power recursions.
